clue.text: Utmost strength possibly could, also the sea

parts.note: 'might' expresses that something possibly could happen
'and' adds something, like 'also'
the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: A remark that the sea might, with all its force, overwhelm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'with might and main' means with every ounce of force one has.

clue.text: Pressing metal in top of grinder

parts.note: iron is a common metal

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of grinder

explanation.surface: A piece of metal pushed into the top of a grinding machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb form for smoothing clothes with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot flat appliance is the household chore of smoothing out creases.

clue.text: Mine host comes from the Loire -which is odd

indicators.note: letters that are odd are strange or out of order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An innkeeper hails from the Loire valley, which seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is odd' rearranges the eight letters of THE LOIRE. 'Mine host' is an old jocular title for an innkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Mine host' is a jocular old phrase for the landlord of an inn or hotel proprietor.

clue.text: Middle of train on Welsh railway line is adrift

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word train is taken

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A train in Wales has come loose from its line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adrift has gone off course, just as plans gone wrong have gone askew.

clue.text: Put off protest over neck wear which is VAT-inclusive

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written over another comes first

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: VAT-inclusive means the tax is included, so the word VAT goes inside the neck wear

parts.note: a tie is worn around the neck

explanation.surface: A protester objects to paying tax on a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclusive' puts VAT inside TIE (TI-VAT-E); 'over' puts DEMO above it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone off is to sap their enthusiasm, removing their drive to act.

clue.text: Girl left a year's record

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl departed, leaving a diary of the year behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is built in answer order, so A comes before L although the clue reads 'left a'.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a chronicle entry recording one year's events; 'annals' are historical records.

clue.text: Sleepwear almost neck wear

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
a tie is worn around the neck

explanation.surface: Bedtime clothing that is nearly a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is a loose garment worn in bed by women and children.

clue.text: This rib is broken by MP when entering Ireland and UK possessions overseas

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are rearranged
the letters MP go into the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
taken as written: a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP breaks a rib while arriving in Ireland, among Britain's old colonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is broken' rearranges THIS RIB; 'when entering' puts MP inside EIRE to make E-MP-IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The territories ruled from London across the globe formed an imperial realm, now largely dissolved.

clue.text: Lord's game to keep on the tarmac at airport

parts.note: cricket is a bat-and-ball game

parts.words: to keep on the tarmac at airport
parts.note: to ground an aircraft is to stop it from flying

explanation.surface: A lord's sport means planes are kept waiting on the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous cricket venue in London; the possessive 's misleads toward a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord's in St John's Wood, London, is the most famous venue for the bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Store or cook domestic fowl

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so these letters are worked into another order

explanation.surface: Keep or roast a farmyard bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is the male of the domestic chicken.

clue.text: Gaffer has one put in feeding box

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a manger is a trough holding fodder for animals
A is one, as the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The boss has a single item placed in the trough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaffer' is British slang for a boss, especially a football club's head coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is British slang for the boss, typically a football club's head coach or a foreman.

clue.text: Front of the hiding place switched round in test

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
turned the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den or hiding place

explanation.surface: The front of a den is turned around during an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched round' turns LAIR into RIAL, placed after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is an examination or experiment to see how something performs.

clue.text: It follows Charlton, for, example, is fit

definitions.meaning: Charlton is a London football club whose full name continues with this word
physically fit, in good sporting shape

explanation.walkthrough: Charlton Athletic is a football club in south-east London; the stray comma after 'for' is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlton's football club takes this word as its suffix, and the adjective also means sporty and strong.

clue.text: Soup collector? One certainly tucks away large amounts

definitions.text: One certainly tucks away large amounts

parts.note: stock is the broth that soup is made from
a piler is one who piles things up, collecting them

explanation.surface: A soup gatherer is someone who eats huge helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks away' suggests eating, but here it means hoarding supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder accumulates large reserves of goods and keeps them stored away.

clue.text: Imply I've become indecent

parts.note: to suggest is to imply
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone hints that they have turned rude.
explanation.definitionFit: A risqué remark hints at something improper, so it is mildly indecent.

clue.text: Pronounced top dog

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: The declared champion canine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese, a small long-haired toy breed from China, is shortened in everyday speech.

clue.text: Birdman goes round church with faithful attendant

indicators.note: one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a hen-man, read as a man of birds

explanation.surface: A bird-keeper walks around the church with a loyal helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' puts CH inside HENMAN, a punning 'bird man' (also the British tennis player Tim Henman).
explanation.definitionFit: A henchman is a loyal follower or right-hand man.

clue.text: The Spanish have a new style and vigour (from France)

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Spaniards have a fresh fashion and French verve.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan, a word borrowed from French, means flair, dash and energy.

clue.text: Piece of publicity about swirling river turned up

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement

indicators.note: letters swirling are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A promotion features an eddying river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' turns RIVER into RRIVE, which 'about' places inside AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To have arrived is to have come to a place, appearing at last.

clue.text: Spreading around a small amount

explanation.definitionFit: A scattering is both the act of strewing things about and a sparse sprinkling of something.

clue.text: Elected friends as residents

parts.note: a candidate elected is in office
mates are friends

explanation.surface: Voted-in pals become the local occupants.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates are those who live in an institution such as a prison or hospital.

clue.text: On the level, nicks vegetables

parts.note: at par means level or equal
snips are small cuts or nicks

explanation.surface: Honestly, someone steals the greens.
explanation.definitionFit: These pale root crops are vegetables related to the carrot.

clue.text: Central point of the senior service, reportedly

indicators.note: as reported in speech, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: the Royal Navy is the senior service, so its adjective is naval

explanation.surface: The navy's main purpose, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The senior service' is the Royal Navy, oldest of Britain's armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button sits at the middle of the body, hence a centre or hub.

clue.text: Arrived with old brooch

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: Someone turned up wearing an antique pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a carved relief brooch, typically a profile on a contrasting background.

clue.text: Once you are seen in it, house prices fall

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the following words

explanation.surface: When you appear in it, property values drop.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'iT HOUse'; 'Once' marks an archaic word for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the old second-person singular pronoun, as in older English and the Bible.

clue.text: Vivian, not Ian, appears in genuine new production of play

indicators.note: one piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: the letters IAN are taken away from Vivian

explanation.surface: Vivian, rather than Ian, stars in a fresh staging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes IAN from VIVIAN to leave VIV, which 'appears in' places inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A revival is a fresh staging of a play not performed for some time.

clue.text: Henry upset top man in London district

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: knocked over, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Henry knocks over the boss in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges TOP MAN into AMPTON. Hampton is a district of south-west London, home of Hampton Court Palace, linked to Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampton, by the Thames in the borough of Richmond, is a suburban area of the capital.

clue.text: Role sounds so unusual for a grieving state

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor's part sounds strange for someone in mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolorous means sorrowful, so this noun names the condition of sorrow.
